subject.summary: Four-step web registration, walked in a mobile browser at 390px wide. The final submit was not pressed.
evidence: live pages walked with a browser tool

lenses.reason: Forms, errors and step transitions were observed.
Covered only through the error-message rule; no screen-reader run.
No persuasive mechanism in the flow.
No goal or content question beyond the usability findings.
No permission or destructive action before the final submit.

steps.title: Enter the email code
steps.reason: Needs the account to be created and a code from an inbox the agent cannot open.

category_health.summary: 2 major (form cleared on Back, F03; vague email error, F07), 1 moderate (label does not match destination, A13R), 2 minor (F09, F04 not assessable).

missing_context.text: Step 5 (email code) and the account-created state were not reached: the final submit was not pressed.
missing_context.resolves_with: A test account or a staging environment with an inbox the agent can read.

missing_context.text: Screen-reader announcement of the email error was not checked.
missing_context.resolves_with: A VoiceOver or TalkBack pass over step 1.

top3.text: Keep step 1 values when the person goes back.
Rewrite the email error to say what is missing.

usability/core.md#A13R.text: A button or link's label text matches, word-for-word, the heading of the screen or section it navigates to. Distinct from N07R, which addresses broader terminology/synonym consistency across a product, not a specific control's exact string matching its own destination's heading.

usability/core.md#F03.text: Previously entered information is not requested again in the same process unless essential/security-related; reuse or offer selection.

usability/core.md#F04.text: The correct keyboard/input mode, autocorrect, autocapitalization, and autocomplete behavior is used for each field.
usability/core.md#F04.sources: Baymard mobile checkout forms, Touch Keyboard Types Cheat Sheet

usability/core.md#F07.text: Validation errors appear next to the source, remain visible, use plain language, and explain how to fix the problem.
usability/core.md#F07.sources: WCAG 2.2 Error Suggestion (SC 3.3.3); NN/g Error-Message Guidelines; Apple HIG Writing; Baymard Ecommerce Checkout UX Guide

usability/core.md#F09.text: Required/optional status is unambiguous and consistent throughout the flow.
usability/core.md#F09.sources: Baymard mobile checkout forms, form design best practices

findings.title: Back from step 2 clears the account form
findings.observation: After Continue on step 1, pressing Back on step 2 shows the account form empty. The email and password must be typed again.
findings.why_it_matters: People who go back to fix one field must re-enter everything, and some give up.
findings.recommendation: Keep the entered email (and keep the password for the session) when the person returns to step 1.
false_positive_conditions: The form clears the password on purpose for security, and the email is kept.
validation_method: Fill step 1, continue, press Back, and check each field.

options.text: Restore the email and password from the current session when step 1 is shown again. Small front-end change.
Restore only the email and ask for the password again, with a note that says why. Keeps the password out of session storage.

picture.caption: The dashed frame marks the email field: empty after Back, although it was filled before Continue.

findings.title: Email error says "Invalid input"
findings.observation: After leaving the email field with "anna.k@example", the error reads "Invalid input". It does not say what is wrong or how to fix it.
findings.why_it_matters: People cannot tell which part of the address is wrong and retry by guessing.
findings.recommendation: Say what is missing and show the expected form: "Add the domain ending, for example anna@example.com."
false_positive_conditions: The message is only a placeholder in a test build and production copy is different.
validation_method: Enter three invalid addresses (no @, no domain ending, a space) and read each message.

options.text: Write one message per error type that says what is missing and shows an example. Copy change plus a small validation split.
Use one general message that shows the expected form: "Enter an email like anna@example.com." Copy change only.

picture.caption: The frame marks the error text under the email field.

panels.title: Step 1
panels.html:

findings.title: "Verify email" leads to "Choose your plan"
findings.observation: The step 2 button reads "Verify email". It opens a screen headed "Choose your plan"; no email is verified.
findings.why_it_matters: The label promises a different next step, so people wait for an email or think they skipped something.
findings.recommendation: Label the button with its destination: "Continue to plan".
false_positive_conditions: The plan screen also sends a verification email and says so.
validation_method: Check whether any request on this transition sends an email.

options.text: Rename the button to "Continue to plan". One string.
Rename the plan screen heading to match a single wording across steps, and label every Continue button with its destination. Copy pass over four screens.

picture.caption: The frame on the left marks the button; the frame on the right marks the heading it leads to.

findings.title: Country has no required or optional mark
findings.observation: Full name and Country show no required or optional status; Country defaults to "Select…".
findings.why_it_matters: People cannot tell whether they may skip the field until an error appears.
findings.recommendation: Mark optional fields "(optional)" and leave required ones unmarked, the same way on every step.
false_positive_conditions: Both fields are required and the form says "All fields are required" above them.
validation_method: Submit step 2 with Country unset and see whether it is accepted.

options.text: Mark each optional field "(optional)" on every step. Copy change on two screens.

findings.title: Email code entry not reviewed
findings.observation: Step 4 says a 6-digit code is sent by email. The code screen was not reached, so its keyboard, autofill and paste behavior are unknown.
findings.why_it_matters: A code field without numeric input and one-time-code autofill slows the last step of registration.
findings.recommendation: Use a numeric one-time-code field that accepts paste and autofill.
false_positive_conditions: The code field already uses numeric input with one-time-code autocomplete.
validation_method: Walk the flow with a test account and a staging inbox, and capture the code screen.

options.text: Use a single numeric field with one-time-code autocomplete that accepts a pasted code. Small front-end change.
